Consult Summary:
- 30-year-old female with 7 days of fever, alternating chills and sweats, myalgias, nausea, poor appetite, and fatigue without clear localizing symptoms.
- Recent travel to Vietnam (returned 4 weeks ago) with rural exposure; malaria prophylaxis taken but regimen unknown. Plan for urgent in-person exam and blood tests including malaria screen.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Febrile illness of unknown origin
  - Timeline: Onset ~7 days ago; persistent.
  - Symptoms: Fever with alternating hot/cold sweats (including night sweats), generalized myalgias, nausea, reduced oral intake, fatigue. Partial, temporary relief with ibuprofen and paracetamol.
  - Pertinent negatives: No cough, sore throat, ear pain, diarrhea, neck stiffness, dysuria, urinary frequency, rash, or joint swelling/tenderness. Headache not worse than baseline.
  - Travel history: Returned from Vietnam 4 weeks ago; mixed urban and rural exposure with trekking/cycling through farmland. Took malaria prophylaxis (daily; possibly more than one agent); unable to recall names.
  - Occupation impact: Difficulty working due to fatigue (works as a nurse).
  - Differential considerations discussed: Malaria and other travel-related infections; occult bacterial/viral infection.
  - Plan discussed: Urgent in-person assessment and blood tests including thick and thin blood films for malaria and inflammatory markers; urgency to be guided by examination findings.

Issue 2:
- Chronic back pain
  - History: Long-standing; associated with prolonged sitting and posture.
  - Current care: Under physiotherapy; focus on posture correction and back muscle strengthening.
  - No current acute exacerbation reported.

Issue 3:
- Recurrent headaches
  - History: Long-standing, typically related to screen use and weather/pressure changes; sometimes migraines.
  - Current status: Not worse than usual; no red flag features reported in this encounter.

Medications:
- Seroxat — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Ibuprofen (over-the-counter) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Paracetamol (over-the-counter) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Malaria prophylaxis during travel — specific agents/regimen not recalled by patient.

Allergies:
- Pollen (hay fever). No medication allergies reported.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic back pain.
- No other major illnesses reported.
- Family history: Father died of myocardial infarction at age 68.

Social History:
- Occupation: Nurse.
- Smoking: Non-smoker.
- Alcohol: Moderate intake.
- Exercise: Moderate activity a few times per week.
- Recent travel: Vietnam; returned 4 weeks ago; rural/urban exposure with trekking and cycling.

Preventative History:
- Vaccinations: Up to date including Hepatitis B (per patient).
- Other preventive screenings (cervical screening test, mammogram, prostate blood test, fecal occult blood test, bone mineral density, eye/skin checks): Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Examination: Not performed (telehealth). In-person exam planned.

Plan:
- Arrange urgent in-person clinical assessment today at central London clinic; alternatively attend local Emergency Department (A&E) if clinic attendance is not feasible.
- Order blood tests after exam, including:
  - Thick and thin blood films for malaria.
  - Inflammatory markers.
- Admin to book urgent appointment; patient to call number provided in consultation notes to confirm slot.
- Work advice: Do not attend work until evaluation completed and cause clarified.
- Further management and urgency of tests to be determined following physical examination.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals, physical exam, medication doses/routes/frequencies, comprehensive medication reconciliation, drug allergies confirmation, pregnancy status, last menstrual period, detailed travel prophylaxis names/regimen, COVID-19 exposure/testing status, hydration status guidance not documented.
- Internal conflicts: None noted. Malaria prophylaxis details uncertain (patient reports daily dosing and possibly an additional medication).
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor pauses/ellipses; adequate clinical content for triage and initial planning.
